html:
La Violencia was a decade of civil war between the supporters of Colombia's Liberal and Conservative parties, from 1948 to 1958. Some 200,000 people were killed, most of them peasants.

It grew from old party hatreds and exploded after the murder of Gaitán in the Bogotazo. Conservative governments used police and gunmen to drive Liberals off their land, and Liberals formed guerrilla bands. In the coffee country and the plains, killings were often savage. Many people fled to the cities.

In 1953 General Gustavo Rojas Pinilla took power and offered amnesty, and in 1958 the two parties formed the National Front, agreeing to alternate the presidency. Peace came between the parties, but some armed peasant groups became the communist guerrillas of the FARC, continuing the Colombian conflict in Colombia.
sum: La Violencia was a decade of civil war between the supporters of Colombia's Liberal and Conservative parties, from 1948 to 1958. Some 200,000 people were killed, most of them peasants.
